title: Where Our Steering Checks Meet Prior Work
summary: Primary-source positioning dossier for the five-check falsification protocol against the 2026 steering-vector reliability literature. Verdict on the protocol: an equivalent-in-kind checks-suite for a safety score IS already published (arXiv:2607.28685 validity audit with pre-specified positive/negative controls and leave-one-organization-out; arXiv:2605.06161 policy invariance with an explicit wording-vs-semantics discrimination requirement), so the checks-suite framing and the discrimination requirement must both be conceded; the residual is the object audited (a benchmark-free, model-level, activation-derived score). The random-direction-null reconciliation with arXiv:2602.06801 is RECONCILED on four legs, one decisive: their orthogonal test steers with v+v_perp, never with v_perp alone, and refusal appears zero times in their full text. The top refutation risk is new and was not on the plan's radar: arXiv:2603.22061 shows a contrast-set manipulation renders a refusal direction functionally inert via magnitude collapse, matching our axis-B norm 2.6-2.7 vs axis-A 10.3-10.6 signature; it must be controlled by a matched-norm re-run before the paper is drafted.
answer:
SATURATION VERDICT FOR THE PROTOCOL: adjacent work exists, and an equivalent-in-kind checks-suite for a safety score is already published — closer than the plan assumed. Two papers force concessions. arXiv:2607.28685 treats safety scores as measurements, separating "construct validity (what a score measures), metric validity (whether its metric measures that target), and criterion validity (whether it tracks held-out behavior)" [8], runs a pre-specified positive control ("MMLU loads 0.74>=0.6") and a negative control (a column-permuted score matrix inside the parallel-analysis null), and reports a contrast that "survives leave-one-organization-out and organization-clustered bootstrap analyses" [8] — the published counterpart of our check (4) jackknife. arXiv:2605.06161 operationalises "rubric-semantics invariance under certified-equivalent rewrites" [9] — the counterpart of our check (1) — and states the discrimination requirement outright: judges "respond to meaningful normative shifts and to meaningless structural rewrites with comparable strength, and cannot tell the two apart" [9]. Both the checks-suite framing and the discrimination requirement are therefore prior art in kind, and any sentence claiming either as novel must be withdrawn. What survives is the object audited: every published audit in this lane validates a behavioural benchmark [8], an LLM scorer [9], or a steering method [3, 4, 12]; none validates a benchmark-free, model-level scalar read off a model's own activations, which is the class alpha_50 belongs to.

RECONCILIATION VERDICT: RECONCILED, on four independent legs, one of them decisive. arXiv:2602.06801 does not contest our norm-matched random-direction null because (i) it never studies refusal — a case-insensitive search for "refus" over the full text returns zero matches — and its five traits ("formality, politeness, sentiment, truthfulness and agreeableness") are continuous classifier scores normalised to the zero-to-one range, i.e. modulation of an expressed attribute rather than induction of an absent behaviour [1, 2]; (ii) its criterion is graded, "Cohen's d as the primary metric throughout, using the threshold |d| < 0.2" [1], not a 50% rate; (iii) decisively, its orthogonal test compares steering with "v + v_perp versus v alone" and never steers along v_perp by itself, whereas our null steers a random direction alone with no refusal component present [1]; and (iv) its sweep is in raw coefficients, "alpha in {0.0,0.5,1.0,2.0,3.0}", with no activation-norm normalisation reported, so conversion to NORM_L units is NOT DERIVABLE FROM PRIMARY TEXT and the magnitude leg is marked unverified [1]. One qualifier should be stated pre-emptively rather than left to a reviewer: their Appendix B finds "Orthogonal perturbations induce logit shifts that are 27-53% smaller than random directions of the same norm" (R = 0.47-0.73) [2], so a norm-matched random direction does move the output distribution; our claim is only that this movement does not cross a behavioural refusal threshold on benign prompts.

THE TOP REFUTATION RISK IS NEW AND WAS NOT ON THE PLAN'S RADAR. arXiv:2603.22061 reports that changing only the construction of the contrast set "produces no functional refusal directions at any tested weight level on any tested layer, while unmatched contrast on the same model, same extraction code, and same evaluation protocol achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers", and attributes it to a magnitude collapse — "reducing the extracted direction magnitude below the threshold at which weight-matrix projection perturbs the residual stream" [7]. Our axis B has norm 2.6-2.7 against axis A's 10.3-10.6: the same signature. Independently, the Braun thesis reports that low-reliability datasets "display smaller means and variances" in activation-difference norms [3], and arXiv:2603.13359 argues directions must be whitened "so that ... a unit of steering has a comparable effect regardless of direction" [5]. This is a published, mechanistic rival explanation for our headline, and it is settled by one cheap experiment: re-run the axis-B sweep with both axes rescaled to unit or matched norm. If B still never crosses, the lexical reading survives and is stronger for having beaten the rival; if B crosses, the headline reduces to arXiv:2603.22061's result. This must be run before the paper is drafted.

arXiv:2602.02132 survives extraction as a real but scope-limited threat, ranked second. All eleven of its refusal directions drive over-refusal on benign prompts to 0.88-1.00 (Gemma alpha=100, Llama alpha=2.5), including pairs that are near-orthogonal (cos = 0.127) or anti-aligned (cos = -0.062), and none fails; in prose, "as steering strength increases, the model increasingly refuses prompts—including benign ones—across datasets" [6]. The target leg therefore does not dissolve the tension and the magnitude leg is unconvertible (no activation norm is reported anywhere). What reconciles it is construction: all eleven directions are estimated from behaviour-labelled prompt contrasts at "the chat-template token immediately preceding the assistant's response (index -2)" [6], whereas our axis B is estimated from paraphrased refusal wording. Their claim is that among behaviour-derived directions geometric identity barely matters; ours is that a wording-derived paraphrase axis is not such a direction. These are compatible, and their result arguably sharpens ours — but it also means a failure to steer cannot be explained by direction identity, which is precisely why risk R1 above is dangerous. Note their directions are unit-normalised by construction [6], which removes the magnitude variable from their result but not from ours.

Both attribution corrections the plan anticipated are confirmed against full texts. The how-not-whether claim belongs to arXiv:2602.02132 — "The primary effect of different directions is not whether the model refuses, but how it refuses" [6] — and no equivalent claim exists in arXiv:2603.13359, whose headline is control ("reduces benign over-refusals by 13.70% and increases harmful refusals by 14.17%") [5]. And arXiv:2602.17881 is a "Master's Thesis, University of Tuebingen. 89 pages, 34 figures", with portions published at the ICLR 2025 Workshop on Foundation Models in the Wild [3] — cite it as a thesis. Three further metadata corrections are recorded (author lists, version pinning for the four-version arXiv:2602.06801, and a 24-vs-25 concept-family discrepancy inside arXiv:2604.15557)), and venue claims were verified independently against the arXiv API rather than taken from secondary listings, confirming ICML 2026 for Interpretability Can Be Actionable and ACL 2026 main conference for the mechanistic-interpretability auditability position paper [11].

Two findings cut in our favour. First, LAP would NOT have predicted alpha_50's failure ex ante, so the plan's optional "independent ex-ante predictor agrees with us" sentence must not be written: A_lin is computed from the prompts, hidden states and frozen unembedding alone, so the steering direction never enters the formula and two lexically distinct axes for one concept receive an identical score; refusal is not among the 24 scored families and appears only as a demo where "the refusal direction has separability 0.988 at the middle layer"; and A_lin is validated only "on single-token next-token completion tasks", which a refusal generation is not [4]. That is a genuine residual for our check (1) rather than a cross-reference. Second, the iter-2 tension with Galeone's functional criterion weakens: arXiv:2604.02608 finds across "12 tasks, 6 models from 3 families, and 4,032 directed cross-template pairs" that steering "routinely succeeds where the logit lens cannot decode the correct answer at any intermediate layer, while the converse — decodable without steerable — is nearly empty (3 of 72)" [10]. A direction that steers without detecting well is the documented common case, so our 0.69-AUROC steering axis is unremarkable rather than anomalous.

On the Braun thesis specifically, one planned question is answered negatively and one number is withheld. It prescribes no layer-span or layer-sensitivity diagnostic — its diagnostics are computed at a fixed layer 13, and the only layer-transfer statement is a description of prior work — so our check (3) is not anticipated there [3]. But no numeric per-predictor correlation appears in its running text (the figures carry them), so it is marked NOT FOUND IN PRIMARY TEXT and no correlation should be quoted for that thesis in the paper.

CONFIDENCE. High for everything read from primary full text via repeated grep: all arXiv:2602.06801 numbers and its zero refusal matches; arXiv:2602.02132's Table 2 over-refusal rates, cosine matrix, alpha grid and token position; arXiv:2604.15557's A_lin definition, three regimes and refusal-demo status; arXiv:2603.13359's percentages and whitening rationale; arXiv:2603.22061's mechanism; and the two saturation papers' abstracts confirmed against body text. Medium for arXiv:2602.17881, where contribution statements are verbatim but numeric correlations were not located. Low for the Adebayo saliency lineage, surfaced only through search summaries and not re-read in primary form — cite it from the NeurIPS 2018 paper before quoting [13]. Caveat: scholarly-mode APIs were unusable on this topic and the arXiv API plus general web search carried the saturation check, so ACL-Anthology-only and OpenReview-only venues are under-sampled; the verdict reads as "the closest equivalents found are these", which is weaker than "no closer equivalent exists".

saturation_F.residual: Our candidate residual (i) survives only in a narrowed form and (ii) does not survive at all. (i) 'The checks are applied to a benchmark-free SAFETY SCORE rather than to an explanation or a steering method' SURVIVES: 2607.28685 audits behavioural benchmarks, 2605.06161 audits an LLM scorer, 2602.17881/2604.15557/2603.24543 audit steering methods; none audits a model-level scalar read off activations. (ii) 'The protocol is required to DISCRIMINATE (pass our-AMS, fail alpha_50) rather than only to condemn' DOES NOT SURVIVE as a novel requirement: 2605.06161's central diagnosis is exactly that judges cannot tell meaningful from meaningless perturbation apart, and 2607.28685 runs pre-specified positive and negative controls that both pass. Rewrite the novelty claim to the object audited plus the specific battery composition, and cite both papers as the methodological precedent.

reconciliation.target_axis: Ours: INDUCING refusal where the default is compliance, on BENIGN prompts, at a 50% rate. Theirs: MODULATION of five continuously-scored stylistic/cognitive traits ('formality, politeness, sentiment, truthfulness and agreeableness', 2602.06801 Sec 6.1), measured by pre-trained classifiers 'normalized to [0,1]'. Refusal is absent from the paper entirely (0 matches for 'refus' in the full HTML v4).
reconciliation.magnitude_axis: UNVERIFIED. Theirs: raw coefficients, 'sweeping steering strength alpha in {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0}' (Sec 6.4), with 'alpha <= 3' as the linearisation scope (App. C.5). No activation-norm normalisation is reported in any main experiment, and no numeric activation norm is given, so conversion to NORM_L units is NOT DERIVABLE FROM PRIMARY TEXT. Ours: alpha in [0,2] NORM_L units, the same calibration family as Rogue Scalpel's alpha = c*mu^(l), c in {0.25..2.0}.
reconciliation.criterion_axis: Theirs is GRADED: 'We report Cohen's d as the primary metric throughout, using the threshold |d| < 0.2 (negligible effect) to indicate behavioral equivalence' (Sec 6.1). Ours is THRESHOLDED: a 50% refusal RATE. Equivalence on a graded effect measure is compatible with every class member sitting below a rate threshold.
reconciliation.intervention_axis_DECISIVE: Their orthogonal test retains the working vector and adds a perturbation: 'we generate n random unit vectors v_perp orthogonal to v via Gram-Schmidt and evaluate steering with v + v_perp versus v alone' (Sec 6.2). They never steer along v_perp alone. Our null steers a norm-matched random direction BY ITSELF, with no refusal component present. The two experiments do not overlap in construct at all. This leg alone settles the reconciliation.
reconciliation.qualifier_to_state_preemptively: Their Appendix B logit-level control finds R = ||l(v)-l(v+v_perp)||_2 / ||l(v)-l(v_rand)||_2 ranges 0.47-0.73, i.e. 'Orthogonal perturbations induce logit shifts that are 27-53% smaller than random directions of the same norm'. A norm-matched random direction therefore DOES move the output distribution; our claim is only that it does not cross a behavioural refusal threshold on benign prompts.
reconciliation.paragraph: Our norm-matched random-direction null - refusal induction between 0.00 and 0.058 across alpha in [0, 2] NORM_L units on benign prompts, with the stylistic axis C returning exactly 0.00 - may appear to sit awkwardly beside the report that steering vectors are non-identifiable because 'orthogonal perturbations achieve near-equivalent efficacy with negligible effect sizes' (Venkatesh and Kurapath, arXiv:2602.06801). It does not, on four counts. Target. That work studies five stylistic and cognitive traits - 'formality, politeness, sentiment, truthfulness and agreeableness' (Sec 6.1) - scored by classifiers 'normalized to [0,1]'; refusal is not among them, and the word does not appear in the paper. Their measurement is modulation of an attribute the model already expresses; ours is induction of a behaviour that is absent by default on benign prompts. Intervention. Their orthogonal test compares steering with v + v_perp against steering with v alone (Sec 6.2): the working direction is retained and a perturbation is added to it. We steer along a random direction by itself, with no refusal component present. The two constructs do not overlap. Criterion. Theirs is graded - 'Cohen's d as the primary metric throughout, using the threshold |d| < 0.2' (Sec 6.1) - while ours is a hard 50% refusal rate. Equivalence on a graded effect measure is fully compatible with every member of an equivalence class sitting below a rate threshold. Magnitude. Their sweep is in raw coefficients, alpha in {0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 3.0} (Sec 6.4), with no activation-norm normalisation reported, so a conversion into our NORM_L units is not derivable from their text; we therefore rest the reconciliation on target, intervention and criterion, and mark the magnitude leg unverified. What our null claims is only this: norm-matched random directions do not induce refusal on benign prompts at alpha <= 2 NORM_L, so the axis-A effect is not an instance of 'any direction steers'. What it does not claim is that the refusal axis is unique or identifiable; the equivalence class of arXiv:2602.06801 is compatible with our null and we do not contest it.

attribution_corrections.wrong: arXiv:2603.13359 claims category-specific directions change HOW not WHETHER a model refuses.
attribution_corrections.right: That claim belongs to arXiv:2602.02132: 'The primary effect of different directions is not whether the model refuses, but how it refuses' [abstract], expanded in Sec 1. Searching 2603.13359 for any equivalent claim returns NOT FOUND IN PRIMARY TEXT; its headline is control ('reduces benign over-refusals by 13.70% and increases harmful refusals by 14.17%', Sec 1). Confirmed against both full texts.
attribution_corrections.consequence: 2602.02132, not 2603.13359, is the nearest published neighbour of the wording-not-behaviour headline.

attribution_corrections.wrong: arXiv:2602.17881 cited as a conference/workshop paper.
attribution_corrections.right: 'Master's Thesis, University of Tuebingen. 89 pages, 34 figures. Portions of this work were published at the ICLR 2025 Workshop on Foundation Models in the Wild (see arXiv:2505.22637)' [arXiv comment field]. Sole author Joschka Braun; supervisors Dr. Seyed Ali Bahrainian and Prof. Carsten Eickhoff, second examiner Prof. Michael Franke [Acknowledgments].
attribution_corrections.consequence: Cite as a thesis, or cite arXiv:2505.22637 for the published portions.

attribution_corrections.right: arXiv:2602.06801 is by Sohan Venkatesh and Ashish Mahendran Kurapath, Manipal Institute of Technology Bengaluru; preprint at v4 (6 Feb 2026 -> 1 Apr 2026); no venue claimed. Quote v4 and pin the version.
attribution_corrections.consequence: Version pinning matters: four versions exist.

attribution_corrections.right: arXiv:2604.15557 is by Jayadev Billa, 'Unaffiliated researcher; previously at ISI@USC, Yahoo, Nuance, and BBN'. Preprint. Abstract says 24 controlled binary families, Sec 1 says a design 'using 25 binary concept families'.

arXiv:2603.13359 author order: Rishab Alagharu, Ishneet Sukhvinder Singh, Shaibi Shamsudeen, Zhen Wu, Ashwinee Panda. Affiliations span Algoverse AI Research, CMU, University of Maryland. Preprint, cs.AI, one version.

papers.title: On the Non-Identifiability of Steering Vectors in Large Language Models
papers.venue_or_status: Preprint, v4 (submitted 6 Feb 2026, revised 1 Apr 2026), cs.LG; Manipal Institute of Technology Bengaluru
claim_extracted: Steering vectors are non-identifiable under white-box single-layer access; the equivalence class is the affine subspace v + ker(J_l).
Orthogonal perturbations ADDED TO a working vector leave behaviour equivalent (mean Cohen's d 0.119 Llama / 0.131 Qwen at n=10 seeds).
Equivalence holds across a raw-coefficient steering sweep alpha in {0.0,0.5,1.0,2.0,3.0}.
Vectors from different extraction methods (contrastive vs PCA) are behaviourally equivalent despite cosines from -0.54 to +0.32.
The limitation is representational, not functional - steering still works.

quotes.text: We test whether adding a random direction orthogonal to v changes steering behavior. For each trait and model, we generate n random unit vectors v_perp orthogonal to v via Gram-Schmidt and evaluate steering with v + v_perp versus v alone across 100 held-out test prompts.
With n=10 seeds, mean Cohen's d is 0.119 for Llama and 0.131 for Qwen, well below the negligible-effect threshold.
We report Cohen's d as the primary metric throughout, using the threshold |d| < 0.2 (negligible effect) to indicate behavioral equivalence.
We evaluate on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct ... The steering interventions are applied at the middle layer of each model (layer 16/32 for Llama, layer 18/36 for Qwen).
We study five semantic traits: formality, politeness, sentiment, truthfulness and agreeableness which spans surface-level and cognitive attributes.
We test this by sweeping steering strength alpha in {0.0,0.5,1.0,2.0,3.0} and measuring Cohen's d between v and v+v_perp at each value, across 10 random seeds.
R ranges from 0.47 to 0.73 across all conditions, as reported in Table 5. Orthogonal perturbations induce logit shifts that are 27-53% smaller than random directions of the same norm.

We note that this does not mean steering is ineffective: the experiments confirm that steering vectors reliably shift model behavior in the intended direction. The limitation is representational, not functional.
Our empirical validation covers two models at mid-network layers across five semantic traits.

magnitude_regime.normalised_units_if_stated: NONE in main experiments; App. B uses norm-matched control directions but reports no numeric activation norm

papers.panel_size: 2 models x 5 traits; 50 contrastive pairs per trait; 100 held-out test prompts; 50 orthogonal directions in the null-space-spanning test
headline_numbers: cross-extraction d < 0.27 in all conditions despite cos in [-0.54, +0.32]
bears_on_which_protocol_check: the random-direction null (not a protocol check but the reconciliation target)
check (1) indirectly, as it argues behavioural equivalence cannot identify a direction
papers.relation_justification: No refusal target (0 matches for 'refus'), modulation not induction, graded criterion not a rate threshold, and the intervention is v+v_perp rather than a random direction alone. Magnitude units unconvertible. The four differences are independent; any one would suffice.
papers.point_of_use_sentence: Non-identifiability of steering directions is established for stylistic traits under a graded equivalence criterion [2602.06801 Sec 6.1-6.2]; our null makes the different and compatible claim that a norm-matched random direction alone does not cross a 50% benign-prompt refusal rate at alpha <= 2 NORM_L.

papers.title: Understanding Unreliability of Steering Vectors in Language Models: Geometric Predictors and the Limits of Linear Approximations
papers.venue_or_status: MASTER'S THESIS, University of Tuebingen, 89 pages, 34 figures; portions published at ICLR 2025 Workshop on Foundation Models in the Wild (arXiv:2505.22637). v1, 19 Feb 2026, cs.CL
claim_extracted: Cosine similarity between training activation differences and the resulting steering vector predicts steering reliability.
Better positive/negative separability along the steering direction predicts steering efficacy.
Steering vectors from different prompt types are directionally distinct yet perform similarly and correlate in efficacy across datasets.
Unreliability is attributed to a linear function class being too restrictive for non-linear latent behaviour representations.
Low-reliability datasets show SMALLER means and variances of activation-difference norms.

quotes.text: Directional agreement within the training data, quantified by the cosine similarity between activation differences and the resulting steering vector, is a significant predictor of the subsequent steering vector's success.
The separability of positive and negative example activations along the learned steering vector direction serves as both a conceptual explanation and an empirical predictor for steering efficacy.

Different prompt types generate directionally distinct steering vectors for the same target behavior. Despite these differences, their overall performance is similar, and their reliability and efficacy is correlated across datasets.
My experiments use 36 multiple-choice datasets from the Model-Written Evaluations (MWE) collection ... Each dataset contains 1000 samples.
Results are shown for Llama 2-7B-Chat model, layer 13 and 500 samples per dataset.

datasets exhibiting low steerability rank (indicative of high reliability) are characterized by larger means and variances in their activation differences. Conversely, datasets with low reliability (colored in red) display smaller means and variances.
transferring a vector far from its extraction layer sharply reduces its power
quotes.anchor: [arXiv:2602.17881 Sec 3.1, describing prior work (Rimsky et al.)]

models: Llama-2-13B-Chat and Qwen-14B-Chat discussed as prior work
papers.layers: Fixed layer 13 for the reported experiments; no cross-layer span statistic
papers.behaviours: 36 MWE behaviour datasets (assistant personality, dangerous behaviours, politics/ethics attitudes)

magnitude_regime.conversion_note: Not needed; the thesis's outcome measures are logit-difference deltas, not a coefficient threshold

papers.panel_size: 36 datasets x 1000 samples; 500 samples/dataset in the reported norm analysis; 7 prompt types compared
headline_numbers: NOT FOUND IN PRIMARY TEXT at running-text level: specific per-predictor r/rho values live in figures; the text states only 'a statistically significant correlation' (Sec 5). DO NOT QUOTE A NUMERIC CORRELATION FOR THIS THESIS.
bears_on_which_protocol_check: check (1) lexical disjointness (prompt-type variation is its nearest analogue)
check (4) stability/jackknife (convergence analysis is a partial analogue)
papers.relation_justification: Its prompt-type result (directionally distinct vectors, similar performance) is the closest published relative of our axis-A-vs-B design, and it went the OTHER way: variation in prompt phrasing did NOT kill efficacy. That makes our axis-B failure notable rather than expected - and also feeds refutation risk R1, since Sec 5.4 ties unreliability to SMALL activation-difference norms, exactly our axis-B signature.
papers.point_of_use_sentence: Geometric predictors of steering unreliability - directional agreement among training activation differences, and positive/negative separability along the steering direction - are established across 36 MWE datasets [2602.17881 Sec 1.8], but they are computed at a single fixed layer [Sec 5.4] and prescribe no layer-span criterion, which is what our check (3) adds.

papers.title: Predicting Where Steering Vectors Succeed
papers.venue_or_status: Preprint, v1, 16 Apr 2026, cs.LG; author 'Unaffiliated researcher; previously at ISI@USC, Yahoo, Nuance, and BBN'
claim_extracted: A_lin (logit-lens classification accuracy at each layer) predicts steering effectiveness and layer selection with no training.
Three regimes: A_mlp low = nothing works; A_mlp high but A_lin low (crystallization gap) = nonlinear methods needed; A_lin high = difference-of-means works.
The middle-layer heuristic fails on both demo models while the LAP-recommended layer succeeds.
A_lin is validated only on single-token next-token completion tasks.

quotes.text: A_lin(l) = (1/N) sum_i 1[argmax_v (W_U . LayerNorm(h_l^(i)))_v = t_i] ... This is the logit lens evaluated as classification accuracy over the concept family. No training is required.
peak A_lin predicts steering effectiveness at rho = +0.86 to +0.91 and layer selection at rho = +0.63 to +0.92
The pooled partial correlation controlling for layer index is r = +0.507 (p < 10^-9, n = 130)
Continent has peak A_lin = 0.70 and steers effectively (Delta P = +0.77 on Llama-8B); parity-related concepts with peak A_lin < 0.05 do not steer (typical Delta P < 0.01).
In our refusal demo on Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct (Appendix Q), the refusal direction has separability 0.988 at the middle layer, so difference-of-means works.
We validate lap on single-token next-token completion tasks, where the logit lens gives an unambiguous accuracy metric.
Will steering work? (go/no-go) If peak A_lin < 0.05 across all layers, the concept is not linearly accessible and difference-of-means steering will produce negligib[le effect]

papers.relation_justification: LAP would NOT have predicted alpha_50's failure ex ante, for three independent reasons: (1) A_lin scores a CONCEPT at a LAYER, never a DIRECTION - the steering vector does not appear in Eq. 1, so axis A and axis B for the same concept receive an IDENTICAL A_lin; (2) refusal is not one of the 24 scored families and has no A_lin value or regime, appearing only as a passing demo that succeeds; (3) A_lin is defined only for single-token completion with a correct answer token, which a refusal-vs-compliance generation does not have. DO NOT write the 'independent ex-ante predictor agrees with our post-hoc check' sentence - the condition fails.
papers.point_of_use_sentence: The published ex-ante predictor of steering success scores a concept at a layer rather than a direction - A_lin is computed from the prompts, hidden states and frozen unembedding alone [2604.15557 Eq. 1] - so it cannot in principle distinguish two lexically distinct axes for the same behaviour, which is precisely what our check (1) tests.
not_found: any A_lin value or regime assignment for refusal
any direction-dependent term in the A_lin definition

papers.title: From Refusal Tokens to Refusal Control: Discovering and Steering Category-Specific Refusal Directions
papers.venue_or_status: Preprint, v1, 9 Mar 2026, cs.AI; Algoverse AI Research / CMU / University of Maryland
claim_extracted: Refusal-token fine-tuning induces separable, category-aligned residual-stream directions.
A learned low-rank combination in a ZCA-whitened orthonormal basis gives a single controllable intervention under anisotropy.
The intervention transfers across same-architecture variants without retraining.
Both methods reduce benign over-refusals while increasing harmful refusals.

quotes.text: On average, categorical steering reduces benign over-refusals by 13.70% and increases harmful refusals by 14.17%. The low-rank combination similarly reduces benign over-refusals by 8.93% and increases harmful refusals by 12.86%, while preserving general model capabilities.

we (i) apply Zero-phase Component Analysis (ZCA) Whitening to categorical steering vectors using a benign covariance estimate, (ii) orthonormalize the whitened directions to obtain a decorrelated steering basis (so that directions are in a fair geometry in which a unit of steering has a comparable effect regardless of direction)

When the Low-Rank Combination is transferred to Llama 3 8B Instruct, it reduces over-refusals on 4/5 benign benchmarks and increases refusals on 8/9 harmful benchmarks, and when applied to DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama, it reduces over-refusals on all benign benchmarks and increases refusals on all harmful benchmarks.

models: Refuse-Llama (Llama 3 8B fine-tuned with categorical refusal tokens)
papers.layers: Single optimal layer l*, intervention at the last token: h~ = h + alpha*s
papers.behaviours: 5 refusal categories; benchmarks include CoCoNot Contrast, WildGuard Unharmful, WildJailbreak Adversarial Benign, OR-Bench

magnitude_regime.raw_units: alpha applied to a whitened/orthonormalised direction s
magnitude_regime.normalised_units_if_stated: Directions are whitened and orthonormalised, which is a fairness normalisation across directions but not an activation-norm normalisation of alpha

headline_numbers: transfer: 4/5 benign and 8/9 harmful on Llama 3 8B Instruct
bears_on_which_protocol_check: a methodological caution on our A-vs-B fairness (anisotropy/whitening), not a check counterpart
papers.relation_justification: A control-method paper, not a measurement claim. It does NOT contain the how-not-whether claim (see AC-1). Its one live bearing on us is adversarial: its whitening rationale implies that comparing two directions at matched coefficient is unfair under activation-space anisotropy, which our axis-A-vs-B comparison must answer (risk R5).
papers.point_of_use_sentence: Category-specific refusal directions can be composed for control, reducing benign over-refusals by 13.70% while increasing harmful refusals by 14.17% [2603.13359 Sec 1]; the same work argues directions must be whitened so that 'a unit of steering has a comparable effect regardless of direction' [Sec 3.4], a fairness requirement our matched-coefficient axis comparison must address.
not_found: any claim that direction choice changes refusal STYLE rather than incidence

papers.title: There Is More to Refusal in Large Language Models than a Single Direction
papers.venue_or_status: Preprint, v1, 2 Feb 2026, cs.CL; no venue in comment field
claim_extracted: Eleven refusal/non-compliance categories yield geometrically distinct activation-space directions (cosines 0.4-0.6 typical, several near-orthogonal).
Steering along ANY of them produces nearly identical refusal/over-refusal trade-offs - a shared one-dimensional control knob.
The primary effect of direction choice is HOW the model refuses, not WHETHER.
SAE analysis explains the collapse: a reusable shared refusal core plus a long tail of style/domain-specific latents.
Increasing steering strength raises over-refusal on BENIGN prompts to near saturation for every direction.

quotes.text: linear steering along any refusal-related direction produces nearly identical refusal to over-refusal trade-offs, acting as a shared one-dimensional control knob. The primary effect of different directions is not whether the model refuses, but how it refuses.
as steering strength increases, the model increasingly refuses prompts-including benign ones-across datasets

many directions are substantially dissimilar (typical cosine similarity 0.4-0.6, with several near-orthogonal), indicating that different refusal categories correspond to distinct activation-space directions

we select the steering strength alpha by a simple grid search over a small discrete set (e.g., alpha in {5,10,20,30,60}) on a held-out validation pool, choosing the smallest value that achieves at least a 90% refusal rate on harmful prompts while keeping benign over-refusals below a chosen threshold
let r in R^d denote the normalized refusal direction. Refusal induction is implemented by modifying activations as x_t' <- x_t + alpha r
Activations are extracted at the chat-template token immediately preceding the assistant's response (index -2), which we treat as the model's decision state.
A notable exception is CoCoNot non-safety categories which respond more gradually to steering.
linear steering collapses a rich internal refusal structure into a coarse behavioral knob, underscoring that such interventions are not suitable as principled safety mechanisms
Our analysis is conducted on two instruction-tuned language models.

papers.layers: Fixed mid-layer hook per model; SAE layers 9/20/31 (GemmaScope) and andyrdt/saes-llama-3.1-8b-instruct
papers.behaviours: 11 refusal splits across WildGuardMix, SorryBench, CoCoNot, XSTest

magnitude_regime.raw_units: alpha grid {5,10,20,30,60}; headline table at Gemma alpha=100, Llama alpha=2.5; direction r is unit-normalised
magnitude_regime.normalised_units_if_stated: NONE - search for 'activation norm', '||h||', 'magnitude' returns 0 matches
magnitude_regime.conversion_note: NOT DERIVABLE FROM PRIMARY TEXT. Note Gemma requires ~40x Llama's alpha, an independent echo of cross-model non-transfer of alpha.

papers.panel_size: 2 models x 11 directions; controlled test set of 200 prompts balanced across harmful/benign x refusal/compliance (HR/HC/BR/BC, 50 each); >=32 prompts per class for direction learning
headline_numbers: Gemma over-refusal rate (ORR, benign) at alpha=100 by direction: Humanizing-CCN 0.97, Incomplete-CCN 0.88, Indeterminate-CCN 0.90, Safety-CCN 1.00, Unsupported-CCN 0.96, CrimeAssistance-SB 1.00, HateSpeech-SB 1.00, Inappropriate-SB 1.00, Advice-SB 1.00, SafetyCore-WGM 1.00, OverRefusal-XST 0.98
Unsteered base models attain 50% on all three metrics
Near-orthogonal pairs that still work: SafetyCore-WGM vs Incomplete-CCN cos=0.127; OverRefusal-XST vs Incomplete-CCN cos=-0.062; OverRefusal-XST vs Unsupported-CCN cos=0.099
bears_on_which_protocol_check: check (1) lexical disjointness - the nearest published neighbour AND the main scoped threat to the wording-not-behaviour headline
papers.relation_justification: Their measurement IS benign-prompt refusal induction, so the target leg does NOT dissolve the tension; and their magnitude is unconvertible, so that leg is unverified. What does reconcile it is CONSTRUCTION: all eleven directions are estimated from behaviour-labelled prompt contrasts at the decision-state token, whereas our axis B is estimated from paraphrased refusal WORDING. Their claim is that among behaviour-derived directions, geometric identity barely matters; ours is that a wording-derived paraphrase axis is not such a direction. These are compatible, and their result sharpens ours: if direction identity is nearly irrelevant, an axis that never steers has lost the behaviour somewhere in estimation - which is exactly why refutation risk R1 is dangerous. Their directions are unit-normalised by construction, which removes the magnitude variable from THEIR result but not from ours.
papers.point_of_use_sentence: Eleven geometrically distinct refusal directions, several near-orthogonal (cos as low as 0.127, one pair at -0.062), all drive over-refusal on benign prompts to 0.88-1.00, so that 'the primary effect of different directions is not whether the model refuses, but how it refuses' [2602.02132 abstract, Tables 1-2]; our axis-B failure is therefore not an instance of direction identity mattering, but of a wording-derived axis not being a refusal direction at all.
papers.refutation_risk: If our axis B, rescaled to matched norm and evaluated on benign-prompt induction under their protocol, still fails to cross while their eleven behaviour-derived directions all saturate, our lexicality claim stands. If instead axis B crosses once normalised, the headline reduces to a magnitude artefact of contrast-set construction - which is arXiv:2603.22061's published result, not ours. The decisive evidence is a benign-prompt induction sweep of both axes at matched norm on the same checkpoints.
not_found: any direction that fails to induce benign-prompt refusal

point_of_use_sentences.check_1_lexical_disjointness: The requirement that a measurement respond to meaning and not to wording is not ours: policy invariance demands 'rubric-semantics invariance under certified-equivalent rewrites', and its central finding is that judges 'respond to meaningful normative shifts and to meaningless structural rewrites with comparable strength, and cannot tell the two apart' [2605.06161 abstract]. Galeone et al. propose the cognate functional criterion for steering - that the intervention direction should also detect - and our 0.69-AUROC axis that nonetheless steers is in tension with it, though a cross-behaviour comparison cannot refute it. Ours transposes the invariance test from the scorer's rubric to the steering axis itself, which no prior work does.
point_of_use_sentences.check_2_monotonicity_in_grid_guard: A logistic dose-response is the theoretically indicated form: the target-concept probability 'is increasing in alpha' with 'a sigmoidal shape' [2602.02712 Thm 3.6, Fig. 4, ICML 2026], while the non-monotonic bump of Theorem 3.3 is per-token and off-target. The practically relevant non-monotonicity is empirical coherence collapse at large coefficients [2509.22067].
point_of_use_sentences.check_3_layer_depth_sensitivity: Layer sensitivity is documented - transferring a vector far from its extraction layer 'sharply reduces its power' [2602.17881 Sec 3.1], and the middle-layer heuristic fails outright, with steering at the LAP-recommended layer redirecting completions where 'the middle layer (the standard heuristic) has no effect on either model' [2604.15557 abstract]. Neither predictor would have caught our failure ex ante: A_lin never sees the steering direction [2604.15557 Eq. 1] and the thesis diagnostics are computed at one fixed layer [2602.17881 Sec 5.4]. Our check (3) is a stability requirement on the score, not a prediction about the vector.
point_of_use_sentences.check_4_leave_one_lineage_out_jackknife: Panel-level robustness checks of this shape are established practice in safety-measurement audits: the capability-safety contrast of arXiv:2607.28685 'survives leave-one-organization-out and organization-clustered bootstrap analyses' [abstract], and the same audit shows how easily a small panel manufactures a result, with a correlation moving 'from -0.64 at n=7 to +0.02 at n=18' and 'a quarter of random size-7 subsets' reaching |rho| >= 0.5 [Sec 1]. Our leave-one-lineage-out jackknife is the model-lineage analogue, and we claim it as an adoption, not an invention.
point_of_use_sentences.check_5_scorer_validity_kappa: Auditing the scorer rather than trusting it is now standard: agent-safety judges show 'an order-of-magnitude spread in judge reliability that is invisible to accuracy-only leaderboards', reported via a Policy Invariance Score and Judge Card protocol [2605.06161 abstract]; and a headline metric can reward degenerate behaviour outright - an 'always positive' baseline scores F1 = 0.690 on R-Judge, 'above five of the 21 models that actually discriminate' [2607.28685 abstract].
point_of_use_sentences.lexicality_provisional_form: Contrast-set construction, not direction geometry, is the live variable: changing only the contrast baseline 'produces no functional refusal directions at any tested weight level on any tested layer, while unmatched contrast on the same model, same extraction code, and same evaluation protocol achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers' [2603.22061 abstract]. Our axis B is a second instance of that phenomenon under a different manipulation - token-disjoint paraphrase rather than topic matching - and, like theirs, ours comes with a magnitude collapse (axis norm 2.6-2.7 against 10.3-10.6) that must be controlled before the lexical reading is preferred.
point_of_use_sentences.lexicality_confirmed_form_requires_HL_re: A lexically disjoint but semantically equivalent axis of comparable detection quality, normalised to matched norm, does not induce refusal at achievable magnitude on any of six checkpoints - axis A crosses at 0.88-1.57 axis-contrast units while axis B reaches ~16 without crossing - so a steering-strength score built on the canned axis prices the wording of refusal rather than the behaviour. This is stronger than the known multi-directionality of refusal, under which eleven geometrically distinct and sometimes near-orthogonal directions all drive benign over-refusal to 0.88-1.00 [2602.02132 Table 2]: the failure of our axis B is therefore not explained by direction identity, which that work shows to be nearly irrelevant.

related_work_paragraph: The reliability of steering vectors was mapped in detail during 2026, and our protocol inherits from four strands. Non-identifiability is established: steering vectors admit 'large equivalence classes of behaviorally indistinguishable interventions', with orthogonal perturbations of a working vector leaving Cohen's d at 0.119-0.131, though the authors stress 'the limitation is representational, not functional' [2602.06801 Sec 6.2, Sec 7]. Unreliability has geometric predictors: cosine agreement among training activation differences and positive/negative separability along the steering direction both predict steering success across 36 Model-Written-Evaluations datasets [2602.17881 Sec 1.8, Sec 4.1]. Success is partly predictable ex ante: the Linear Accessibility Profile repurposes the logit lens so that peak A_lin predicts steering effectiveness at rho = +0.86 to +0.91 across 24 binary concept families, though it scores a concept at a layer rather than a direction, and is validated only 'on single-token next-token completion tasks' [2604.15557 abstract, Sec 1, Sec 3.2]. And refusal itself is multi-directional: eleven categories yield geometrically distinct directions, several near-orthogonal, yet 'linear steering along any refusal-related direction produces nearly identical refusal to over-refusal trade-offs', so 'the primary effect of different directions is not whether the model refuses, but how it refuses' [2602.02132 abstract]. Category-specific directions can also be composed for control, reducing benign over-refusals by 13.70% [2603.13359 Sec 1].
residual_novelty_statement: Concessions first, all of them. Steering fragility is known [2602.17881; 2603.24543]. Steering-vector non-identifiability is known, formally and empirically [2602.06801]. Layer sensitivity is known, and the middle-layer heuristic is already published as unreliable [2604.15557]. Ex-ante predictors of steerability exist [2604.15557]. Refusal is known to be multi-directional while behaving as a single control knob [2602.02132]. A checks-suite applied to a safety score exists, with pre-specified positive and negative controls and leave-one-organization-out robustness [2607.28685]. A wording-versus-semantics invariance test for a safety measurement exists, and so does the requirement that the measurement discriminate between the two [2605.06161]. And the observation that contrast-set construction alone can render a refusal direction functionally inert exists [2603.22061]. What remains ours is narrow and should be claimed narrowly: the object audited. Every published audit in this lane validates either a behavioural benchmark [2607.28685], an LLM scorer [2605.06161], or a steering method [2602.17881; 2604.15557; 2603.24543]. None validates a benchmark-free, model-level scalar read off a model's own activations - the class alpha_50 belongs to - and none composes the specific battery we run: an axis-level paraphrase-invariance test, an in-grid monotonic dose-response guard, a layer-span stability gate on the score rather than the vector, a leave-one-lineage-out jackknife over model families, and a scorer-agreement check, evaluated against the requirement that the battery pass one benchmark-free score and fail another. The discrimination requirement is prior art in kind; its instantiation on an activation-derived safety score, and the finding that a published-looking score fails it, is not. Claim that, and nothing wider.

refutation_risks.title: Magnitude-collapse rival explanation for the lexicality headline
refutation_risks.statement: A contrast-baseline manipulation 'produces no functional refusal directions at any tested weight level on any tested layer' while unmatched contrast 'achieves complete refusal elimination on six layers', because topic-matched subtraction cancels the shared component, 'reducing the extracted direction magnitude below the threshold at which weight-matrix projection perturbs the residual stream'. Our axis B norm 2.6-2.7 vs axis A 10.3-10.6 is the same signature.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: Re-run the axis-B sweep with both axes rescaled to unit (or matched) norm before applying alpha, and report whether B still fails to cross. If it still never crosses, the lexical reading survives and is stronger for beating the rival. If it crosses, the headline reduces to arXiv:2603.22061's published result. MUST BE RUN BEFORE THE PAPER IS DRAFTED. If the axis-contrast unit already normalises the axis, state that explicitly in one sentence.

refutation_risks.title: The shared-knob result on benign prompts
refutation_risks.statement: All eleven directions, including pairs at cos=0.127 and cos=-0.062, drive benign over-refusal to 0.88-1.00; none fails. Read naively, direction identity does not matter, so our axis-B failure needs an explanation that is not 'different direction'.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: A benign-prompt induction sweep along their category directions at matched norm alongside our axis B on the same checkpoints, showing axis B is not simply an eleventh behaviour-derived direction. Ranked second only because their directions are unit-normalised by construction, which removes the variable R1 identifies as decisive.

refutation_risks.title: The discrimination requirement is not ours
refutation_risks.statement: Policy invariance already requires a safety measurement to move under semantic change and not under content-preserving rewrites, and names failure-to-distinguish as the diagnosis.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: Nothing - it is settled. Withdraw any sentence claiming the discrimination requirement as novel; keep the object-audited residual.

refutation_risks.title: The checks-suite framing is not ours either
refutation_risks.statement: Pre-specified positive and negative controls plus leave-one-organization-out on safety scores are already published practice.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: Nothing - present our protocol as an instantiation for a new measurement class, not a new methodology.

refutation_risks.title: Anisotropy objection to a matched-coefficient A-vs-B comparison
refutation_risks.statement: A fair cross-direction comparison is argued to require ZCA whitening 'so that a unit of steering has a comparable effect regardless of direction'. An unwhitened matched-coefficient comparison is attackable independently of R1.

refutation_risks.title: The Galeone tension is weaker than iteration 2 feared (CUTS IN OUR FAVOUR)
refutation_risks.statement: Across '12 tasks, 6 models from 3 families, and 4,032 directed cross-template pairs', 'FV steering routinely succeeds where the logit lens cannot decode the correct answer at any intermediate layer, while the converse - decodable without steerable - is nearly empty (3 of 72)'. A direction that steers without detecting well is the documented common case.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: Already settled enough to downgrade the iteration-2 'in tension with' language; cite 2604.02608 as the counterweight and treat the functional criterion as one criterion among competing ones.

refutation_risks.title: The NORM_L defence is incomplete
refutation_risks.statement: A trend 'depends jointly on raw units, the readout metric, and the operating point; correcting any one of these removes it'. NORM_L handles only the units.
refutation_risks.what_would_settle_it: State the readout metric (thresholded refusal rate) and the operating point (alpha_50, a fixed 50% crossing) explicitly, and show the score under a second readout threshold.

pinned_lane_updates.update: Its warning now binds check (3) as well as NORM_L: the paper must name its readout metric and operating point, not only its units. Claim unchanged, obligation added. See refutation risk R7.

DOWNGRADE THE TENSION. arXiv:2604.02608 establishes steerable-not-decodable as the common case ('the converse - decodable without steerable - is nearly empty (3 of 72)'), so our 0.69-AUROC steering axis is unremarkable rather than anomalous. Report the functional criterion as one candidate criterion, cite 2604.02608 as counterweight, drop 'lone counterexample' framing. Claim weakened in our favour.

Unchanged as the product competitor ('presumes an attested reference'). Under the discriminating-protocol framing the sharper comparison is that its AUROC 0.95 on a 273-checkpoint registry is a CRITERION-validity result, which our protocol does not yet supply for alpha_50 or our-AMS. Comparison sharpened.
Unchanged; still the nearest neighbour of alpha_50 as an object.
Unchanged; still endorses the logistic functional form (Thm 3.6 / Fig. 4), ICML 2026.

Iteration-2 follow-up partly answered: intervention is 'h~ = h + m v' with scalar multiplier m applied on the PROMPT tokens [Sec 3], from CAA multiple-choice contrast triples where 'prompts are identical' apart from the answer option; the protocol is a unified evaluation protocol over CAA vectors on JailbreakBench. The multipliers at which the +57%/-50% ASR swings occur remain NOT EXTRACTED, so the c = alpha/||h|| placement is still open.

follow_up_questions: Does axis B still fail to cross the 50% benign refusal rate when both axes are rescaled to unit (or matched) norm before alpha is applied? This is the single decisive experiment: it separates our lexicality claim from arXiv:2603.22061's published magnitude-collapse mechanism, and until it is run the headline has a named rival explanation with a matching numeric signature (axis norms 2.6-2.7 vs 10.3-10.6).

Would our axis B behave like an eleventh direction under the arXiv:2602.02132 protocol - unit-normalised, applied at the decision-state token (index -2) at their mid-layer hook, swept to their alpha regime - or does it remain inert where all eleven of their behaviour-derived directions saturate benign over-refusal at 0.88-1.00?

What is the activation norm ||h|| at gemma-2-9b-it layer 20 and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct layers 15-16, so that arXiv:2602.02132's alpha=100 and alpha=2.5 can be placed on the same c = alpha/||h|| axis as our [0,2] NORM_L grid? Neither that paper nor arXiv:2602.06801 reports an activation norm, so every magnitude comparison in this lane is currently unverifiable from primary text.

Does the five-check protocol survive contact with arXiv:2607.28685's criterion-validity standard - i.e. can we show that a score passing our battery tracks a held-out behavioural criterion on a model panel large enough to avoid the small-panel artefact they document (rho moving from -0.64 at n=7 to +0.02 at n=18)?
confidence: HIGH for everything read from primary full text via repeated grep: all arXiv:2602.06801 numbers and its zero refusal matches; arXiv:2602.02132's Table 2 ORR values, cosine matrix entries, alpha grid and decision-state token; arXiv:2604.15557's A_lin definition, three regimes and refusal-demo status; arXiv:2603.13359's headline percentages and whitening rationale; arXiv:2603.22061's mechanism; arXiv:2605.06161 and arXiv:2607.28685 abstracts plus body confirmations. MEDIUM for arXiv:2602.17881, where the contribution statements and Sec 5.4 norm finding are verbatim but no numeric correlation was located in running text (marked NOT FOUND IN PRIMARY TEXT - do not quote one). LOW/SECONDARY for the Adebayo saliency lineage, which was surfaced through search summaries and not re-read in primary form. Caveat on the saturation check: scholarly-mode APIs (OpenAlex/Crossref) were unusable on this topic and the arXiv API plus general web search carried it, so non-arXiv venues (ACL Anthology-only, OpenReview-only workshops) remain under-sampled; the verdict should be read as 'closest equivalents found are these', which is weaker than 'no closer equivalent exists'.
